name: Trusted production repository sourcing, database topology, and activation-readiness boundary
phase: Discovery and specification only; no implementation or activation authorized
purpose: Record committed production-capable repository sources and the remaining target/configuration/approval decisions without introducing another generic transport or composition abstraction.

food001.capability: prepare(sql) returning bind/all statements; batch(statements) returning FoodD1Result envelopes
food001.construction: Synchronous and I/O-free; raw constructor retains the trusted injected database, not an authorization service.
food001.exactReadProjection: createFoodMenuReadDependencies({ repository }) captures receiver-bound getProduct/getRecipe, preserving raw found/not-found results, promises and failures. No extra repository adapter is needed. Do not project FOOD-001 private-service result envelopes instead.

food002.readDependencies: Pick<FoodDraftRepository, getProduct | getRecipe>; exact historical reads only
food002.construction: Synchronous structural checks; no database or dependency operation during construction. H/L construct this repository internally.

topology.supported: Either shared dedicated food database or separate dedicated food databases through injection; neither is required by domain contracts.
topology.shared: The same FoodD1Database capability can serve both repositories; table names do not collide. FOOD-001 product-to-recipe SQL foreign keys and FOOD-002 internal menu SQL foreign keys remain local to their respective table families.
topology.separate: Acquire trusted FOOD-001 database, construct its repository and Q reads; inject those reads into H/J/L with independently acquired menu database. Existing input types already support this graph.
topology.crossDatabase: FOOD-002 presentation product/recipe coordinates have no physical SQL foreign keys into FOOD-001 tables. Logical exact reads validate dependencies even on shared storage; sharing does not make cross-repository operations an atomic snapshot.
topology.acquisitionScope: acquirePrivateFoodMenuDatabaseFromEnvironment({ environment, bindingName }) acquires one explicitly selected database capability. J uses it for menu storage, not implicitly for all food persistence. A future trusted caller must also acquire the FOOD-001 source; the existing structural acquisition helper can be reused with an approved key without a new abstraction or fallback.

committedConfiguration.targetEvidence: Existing bindings contain concrete production-like target declarations, not food placeholders. Declaration does not prove provisioning, schema state or availability; identifiers and account values are deliberately omitted and no target was queried.
committedConfiguration.foodBinding: No FOOD-001 or FOOD-002 D1 binding is declared. RIVER_FOOD_DB is a FOOD-001F contract/documentary target only.
committedConfiguration.menuBindingNameReadiness: UNRESOLVED: I/J accept a trusted bindingName, but no production menu value or topology has been selected.
committedConfiguration.foodDatabaseTargetReadiness: UNRESOLVED: no dedicated food target is declared; actual existence/provisioning is not verified.
committedConfiguration.administratorKey: RIVER_FOOD_ADMIN_PRINCIPAL_ID is a canonical PrincipalId string contract in FOOD-001F and the activation runbook; absent from committed Wrangler configuration, generated environment declarations and example key sets inspected.
committedConfiguration.typing: worker-configuration.d.ts is generated by wrangler types and declares the four existing D1 bindings. Food keys are absent. Structural injection suffices for current code; regenerate only after separately approved actual binding/config declaration. Do not manually pretend generated types provision resources.
committedConfiguration.environmentSeparation: No food-specific local/dev/production target separation is declared. Separate target configuration and isolated local state must be selected before use.
committedConfiguration.scripts: package.json deploy runs wrangler deploy; publish builds then deploys. No dedicated food migration application script/configuration is present. Existing per-binding migrations_dir declarations support multiple streams but do not select a food stream.

migrations.schemaSourceReadiness: code-complete for FOOD-001 exact reads and FOOD-002 menu repository; excludes future ordering/payment schemas

inventory.constraints: Exact composite product-to-recipe FK, safe integer version bounds, ordering/reference indexes, UPDATE and DELETE rejection triggers; no cascade deletion.

Internal exact composite FKs, safe integer versions/revisions, UTF-16 ordering indexes, stable offer-to-dish trigger, trigger-generated publication memberships, UPDATE and DELETE rejection for all six tables; no cascade deletion.

migrations.sharedOrder: Apply existing 0001 then 0002 in migrations/food after explicit target verification and migration approval. No renaming required. 0002 has no SQL dependency on 0001 tables, but usable menu exact-reference verification requires FOOD-001 schema and records.
migrations.separateOrder: FOOD-001 and menu migration streams can be independent. Existing files share one directory, so selecting separate targets requires an approved stream/application plan; do not blindly point both targets at the whole directory or silently move/rename migrations.
migrations.verification: Committed isolated Miniflare integration tests exercise actual respective migration SQL through convertV4MiniflareOptions, cf:false, d1Persist:false and dispatchFetch worker-side D1 batch. Prior validation reported PASS; this discovery does not rerun SQL or query configured databases.
migrations.configuredLocalApplied: Not established by inspected repository evidence
migrations.remoteProductionApplied: Not established by inspected repository evidence
migrations.limits: Local tests do not establish remote replication consistency, production transport behavior or production migration application. SQL presence and test success are distinct from activation.

futureAssembly.foodSource: Approved trusted environment/key -> acquirePrivateFoodMenuDatabaseFromEnvironment -> new D1FoodDraftRepository(foodDatabase) -> createFoodMenuReadDependencies({ repository })
futureAssembly.menuRuntime: createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeFromServerContext({ environment, bindingName: approvedMenuKey, session: requestSession, readDependencies: qReads, administratorPrincipalId: trustedCanonicalAdministrator, now?: trustedClock })
futureAssembly.internalGraph: J -> I menu acquisition + new AstroPrincipalSessionStore(session, now) + new D1PrincipalRepository(environment.RIVER_IDENTITY_DB) + new DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver({ sessions, principals }) -> L createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeComposition -> one D1FoodMenuRepository(menuDatabase, qReads) -> one SingleAdminFoodMenuService -> workspace plus operationGate from that same service
futureAssembly.transportGraph: createPrivateFoodMenuMutationRequestBoundary({ operationGate: capabilities.operationGate, workspace: capabilities.workspace, expectedOrigin: trustedApprovedOrigin }) -> createPrivateFoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter({ boundary }) -> createPrivateFoodMenuMutationServerHandler({ adapter }) -> handler.handle(context.request); P calls createPrivateFoodMenuMutationResponse for N results.
futureAssembly.authorization: Trusted Q raw reads remain hidden infrastructure. User-facing operations pass through menu authorization; method/origin policy precedes lazy body read, gate authorization precedes parsing, normal mutation resolves authorization again. No token, duplicate administrator policy or FOOD-001 user service is needed for Q.
futureAssembly.construction: All assembly is synchronous and I/O-free. Structural success does not prove target existence/schema/session trust. Actual I/O begins during handle/service operations.
futureAssembly.lifecycle: Prefer per-request/server-context assembly, matching J and endpoint precedents. Repositories retain database/dependency capabilities, not caller session state, and need no invented pooling; raw repository reuse is technically possible but unnecessary here. Never cache request-scoped session/resolver/service/gate/handler state across requests. Sharing one injected D1 object is compatible with both repositories.

trustedSources.administrator: Architecture exists but no food wiring: H documents environment-specific RIVER_FOOD_ADMIN_PRINCIPAL_ID with secret handling recommended for privileged configuration. J accepts an already canonical PrincipalId and does not read that key itself. A future trusted caller must select/configure and parse the value unchanged; compile-time constants, request-supplied roles and River OS boolean auth are not substitutes.
trustedSources.principalVerification: After separate owner approval, verify the intended active principal through the existing identity repository/system against the approved identity target. Do not infer from email, operator cookies, test fixtures or display names. No concrete principal was inspected or selected here.
trustedSources.origin: astro.config.mjs site supplies a committed trusted canonical-site candidate; existing CRM same-origin helper compares Origin with request.url, which is not a selected FOOD-002M expectedOrigin source. Choose an explicit trusted per-environment mapping, never incoming Host/Origin/request URL. No food expected-origin production configuration exists.
trustedSources.session: ALREADY RESOLVED plumbing: Astro APIRoute context.session is request-scoped and reusable as AstroSessionLike. Shared adapter awaits async-or-sync get, preserves synchronous set/delete, asynchronous regenerate and sync-or-async destroy, canonical validation, expiry and fail-closed cleanup.
trustedSources.identity: ALREADY RESOLVED construction contract and binding declaration: J constructs D1PrincipalRepository from RIVER_IDENTITY_DB.prepare and DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver itself. J readDependencies are FOOD-001 exact reads, not identity dependencies. Schema/live identity availability remains a deployment prerequisite, not a construction guarantee.
trustedSources.environment: ALREADY RESOLVED acquisition precedent: committed endpoints import env from cloudflare:workers and inject it into structural runtime adapters. A later route can follow that precedent without changing current pure FOOD modules. No real secret files or remote services were inspected.

routeReadiness.source: Not yet authorized/registered; technically composable using existing contracts once trusted configuration-source decisions are documented. Likely future path src/pages/river-os/actions/food-menu.ts, APIRoute with prerender=false, trusted acquisition/assembly then handler.handle(context.request).
routeReadiness.registration: Astro src/pages automatically registers endpoint source in the next build. Unconfigured source can return sanitized 503 but is not an activation switch; deployment exposes the endpoint even when unavailable. Route addition therefore needs explicit approval separately from deployment/activation; missing configuration does not silently authorize registration.
routeReadiness.unavailablePolicy: Recommend fixed sanitized JSON 503 with no-store at the future route assembly boundary, following Sesh creator profile and private CRM infrastructure precedents. Existing endpoints are not uniformly identical. configuration-unavailable is not a FOOD-002M request result and must not be forced through P as callback-failed. This policy is documentary and requires a separately approved route implementation.
routeReadiness.activation: NOT READY: food targets/configuration/migration application/admin/origin and private activation approval remain unresolved. Route presence or published snapshot state does not authorize public exposure, checkout or sale.

approvalGates: Select environment/account/region/topology and exact targets; no phase authorizes the next.
Provision dedicated targets only after explicit approval; do not reuse unrelated domain databases.
Declare bindings/migration configuration and regenerate types only with explicit repository configuration approval.
Verify remote target and recovery plan, then apply approved migrations only with migration approval.
Verify/configure administrator and select trusted expected origin with owner approval.
Approve private route registration independently of deployment.
Approve deployment and production/private activation separately; preserve FOOD-001H gates.

options: One dedicated food database: existing migrations/food stream and shared capability
Separate dedicated food databases: independent operational isolation and explicit split-stream plan
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Shared dedicated food database is the simplest documentary default supported by FOOD-001H and the current migration directory; owner must choose, and this specification selects neither.

options: Shared menu acquisition uses the intended RIVER_FOOD_DB key
Separate menu key explicitly selected alongside the FOOD-001 key
ownerDecisions.consequence: Keys and real D1 targets are distinct decisions; no concrete names/IDs/account values are supplied here.

options: Owner-verified canonical active PrincipalId through protected environment configuration; canonical site mapped to approved environment
Another explicit trusted server configuration source reviewed before wiring
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Reuse H protected admin configuration guidance and committed site as a candidate, with explicit environment approval and no request-derived trust.

options: Keep route absent until prerequisites are approved
Separately approve source registration with fail-closed 503 before live prerequisites, while withholding deployment/activation
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Keep route absent during this slice; registration and activation are separate approvals.

nextSlice.recommendation: Owner-reviewed food target/configuration and assembly decision slice, documentary only until topology, binding keys, administrator/origin source and activation sequence are approved. Then separately authorize concrete configuration/provisioning/migration and thin route integration phases; do not invent FOOD-002S implementation solely to wrap existing factories.
nextSlice.pureCodeOpportunity: Existing constructors and Q/J/L/M/N/P can be assembled inline in a later thin trusted route; a route-independent assembly test may be useful during that authorized integration, but no unresolved repository-result semantics or mandatory new adapter remains.

strictExclusions: Configured local or remote database access
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly this specification is created; no tracked file changes and nothing staged.
Every referenced file and existing factory signature is checked against committed state; migration and binding inventories match committed source.
Topology support is distinguished from owner selection and target provisioning; no applied-schema claims without evidence.
Q semantic projection is resolved, complete existing assembly is documented, and no unnecessary abstraction is required.
Configuration failure, authorization failure, route registration, deployment and activation remain distinct.
JSON parses, reference checks pass, whitespace checks and git diff --check pass; exact git status is returned.
